name: UB bank conflict ratio is high — apply when vector is bound and aiv_vec_stu_cflt_ratio + aiv_vec_ldu_cflt_ratio + aiv_vec_sfu_cflt_ratio > 0.3
matchText:
UB bank conflict ratio is high — apply when vector is bound and aiv_vec_stu_cflt_ratio + aiv_vec_ldu_cflt_ratio + aiv_vec_sfu_cflt_ratio > 0.3

Trigger condition (summary): with vector bound, aiv_vec_stu_cflt_ratio + aiv_vec_ldu_cflt_ratio + aiv_vec_sfu_cflt_ratio
sum > 0.3: overall bank-conflict stall is high; localize the dominant cause per conflict type below.

Observable symptom: aiv_vec_stu_cflt_ratio + aiv_vec_ldu_cflt_ratio + aiv_vec_sfu_cflt_ratio > 0.3

bank group definition (A5/Atlas 350): the Unified Buffer is organized as banks (equal-sized memory modules). The Unified Buffer is 256K in total, split into 16 banks.
Each bank has 512 rows of 32B each. The 16 banks are further grouped into 8 bank groups, each holding 2 banks; e.g. bank7 and bank15 form one bank group.
bank_index = (addr // 32) % 16, group = bank_index % 8. Address distance that is a multiple of 512B (=32B*16) → same-bank conflict; a multiple of 256B (=32B*8) → same bank-group conflict as well.

Analysis points:
1) Write-write conflict — mapped to aiv_vec_stu_cflt_ratio
Multiple write operations access the same bank group at the same time.
DataBlocks of the vector-instruction destination operand dst spaced by multiples of 256B (=32B*8) → same bank-group conflict.

2) Read-read conflict — mapped to aiv_vec_ldu_cflt_ratio
Two read operations access the same bank, or more than two read operations access the same bank group.
Address distance between two source operands (or across DataBlocks of one source operand) that is a multiple of 512B (=32B*16) → same-bank conflict; a multiple of 256B (=32B*8) → same bank-group conflict as well.

3) Read-write conflict — mapped to aiv_vec_sfu_cflt_ratio
A read and a write operation access the same bank at the same time.
Address distance between the source operand src and the destination operand dst that is a multiple of 512B (=32B*16) → same-bank conflict.

Fixes:
- Optimize the compute order: make the src/dst start-address difference avoid multiples of 256B (same group) and 512B (same bank), landing in different bank groups / different banks. Prefer iterating along the low-dimensional axis of the shape.
- Keep read/write targets row-major and contiguously laid out; avoid column-major access (operand address distance being a multiple of 256B) repeatedly hitting the same group.
- Optimize memory allocation: allocate slightly larger buffers so dst start addresses avoid multiples of 512B (same bank), with the next buffer starting at a non-aligned offset; stack additional offsets that are not multiples of 256B/512B.
